output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: StringLookupFactory.addDefaultStringLookups() registered every DefaultStringLookup enum value — including SCRIPT (ScriptStringLookup -> ScriptEngine.eval), DNS, and URL — into the interpolator used by StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator(). Any string containing `${script:javascript:...}` reached ScriptStringLookup.lookup() (line 86) and executed attacker-supplied code, matching the finder trace.

Fix: In addDefaultStringLookups(), skip the DNS, SCRIPT, and URL lookups via a new private helper isDefaultDisabledLookup(DefaultStringLookup). This mirrors the upstream commons-text 1.10.0 remediation: these interpolators are no longer enabled by default and must be opted into explicitly (e.g. via StringLookupFactory.INSTANCE.interpolatorStringLookup(map, null, true) with the desired lookup placed in the map). Safe lookups (base64, const, date, env, file, java, localhost, properties, resourceBundle, sys, urlDecoder/urlEncoder, xml) remain enabled, so existing legitimate behavior is preserved.

Tests: Updated StringLookupFactoryTest.assertDefaultKeys to assert dns/script/url are absent from the default set and added a StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator() regression asserting the script payload is left unresolved. Updated StringSubstitutorWithInterpolatorStringLookupTest so the dns/javascript functional tests explicitly enable their lookup (new createInterpolatorWith helper), and added testDefaultInterpolatorDoesNotEnableScript. Verified: POV exits non-zero ("NOT VULNERABLE") after patch, and the full suite passes (1222 tests, 0 failures/errors).
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: applications that relied on the `script`, `dns`, or `url` lookups being active in the default interpolator will now see those expressions left unresolved. This is the intended, security-correct default (matches commons-text 1.10.0); such callers must now enable those lookups explicitly. The `urlDecoder`/`urlEncoder` lookups are unaffected and remain enabled. No API signatures changed. Build must run with -Drat.skip=true only because the pre-existing POV source file under .security-pipeline/pov lacks an ASF license header; product code was not touched by that flag.
output_json.summary: Fixed CVE-2022-42889 (Text4Shell / CWE-094) in Apache Commons Text by removing the dangerous `script`, `dns`, and `url` interpolators from the default lookup set used by StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator(). Attacker-controlled `${script:javascript:...}` input is now left unresolved instead of being evaluated by the Nashorn ScriptEngine, blocking arbitrary code execution while preserving all safe default lookups. The lookups can still be enabled explicitly by callers that need them.
